The defining loss is QB Diego Pavia (92.2, Heisman runner-up, graduated) - the engine of the #1 opponent-adjusted offense. He is replaced by true freshman Jared Curtis, the #1 OVERALL recruit (a Georgia flip), who has an elite ceiling but ZERO college experience. Opposing coach: 'they won't be as good without Diego.'

The offense also loses Mackey Award TE Eli Stowers (NFL R2), deep-threat WR Tre Richardson (-> Louisville), and FOUR of five OL starters. The '25 OL was actually poor in pass pro (PBLK p4) - Pavia masked it by scrambling; the rebuild (1 returning starter McConnell + FCS/P4 transfers) pairs an unproven line with a true frosh.

STRENGTHS: RB (Alexander + Young return, 981 combined yds/17 TD), a loaded, experienced SECONDARY (star CB Jordan Matthews 80.1 + two-way Hight + S CJ Heard + Clemson's 6-INT Ricardo Jones), and ELITE special teams (Brock Taylor, a top-5-caliber placekicker; SP+ top ST unit 2 straight years, SPEC p90).

The DL returns 3 starters + NFL-prospect DT Ouattara (injury return) + 5 transfers, but the pass rush is a concern (projected edges Capers + Allen combined for just 5 sacks in '25). Post-Pavia, the market (Athlon NF45, P6 #46) projects a clear regression/rebuilding season.
